page: Microsoft Azure D192lds_v7 is an x86_64 server instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The system is driven by dedicated Intel Xeon 6973P-C processors providing 96 physical cores and 192 vCPUs clocked at 4.2 GHz. The processor architecture includes a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and advanced instruction sets including Intel AMX and AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 support. Memory capacity is configured at 384 GB, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM allocation. Ephemeral storage is bundled as an 11,340 GB NVMe SSD array. Discrete GPUs are not present on this instance type.

Performance testing places the multi-threaded compute and memory subsystem in the top 10 percent of evaluated machines. The instance achieved 202,853.75 on multi-core stress-ng and 152,145.2 on PassMark CPU evaluations, alongside a cached small-block read bandwidth of 15,083.08 GB/s and uncached large-block read speeds of 688.55 GB/s. High data throughput is further reflected in static web serving benchmarks at 157.94 GB/s and Redis performance reaching 268.62 million SET operations per second. Single-core compute capability remains within the median tier, measuring 2,289.99 in stress-ng.

Given the high core density and 11.34 TB of bundled NVMe storage, the hardware profile offers strong cost efficiency for parallel execution that does not require massive memory per thread. The 2 GB per core ratio represents an architectural tradeoff, prioritizing high CPU density and local NVMe throughput over large in-memory footprints. The configuration is suited for compute-heavy batch processing, distributed caching layers, data transformation pipelines, and high-IOPS local database engines.
description: Microsoft Azure D192lds_v7 is a high-density instance powered by Intel Xeon 6973P-C processors based on the x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V. The hardware configuration delivers 192 dedicated vCPUs across 96 physical cores at 4.2 GHz, backed by 480 MB of L3 cache and support for AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets. System memory is sized at 384 GB, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, paired directly with 11,340 GB of local NVMe SSD storage with zero discrete GPUs. Benchmark results demonstrate top-decile multi-core processing power, top-tier uncached read bandwidth of 688.55 GB/s, and key-value throughput reaching 268.62 million Redis operations per second. Although single-threaded execution registers in the median range, the combination of substantial thread concurrency and fast local NVMe capacity makes the server an efficient choice for compute-intensive batch tasks, large-scale ETL pipelines, and high-throughput database workloads.
